title: Quaternionic division points on curves in the Siegel threefold
main_claim: A Hodge-generic irreducible curve C in A_2 over Qbar contains only finitely many points whose full geometric endomorphism algebra is an indefinite quaternion division algebra over Q. This is the QM part of Zilber-Pink for curves in A_2, with no boundary hypothesis. The proof bounds heights polynomially in degree for QM points using G-function interpolation at an interior QM centre, with the trace constants eliminated by Frobenius pairing. A Pila-Zannier count then finishes it.

issues.location: Sec. 4, Prop. prop:nonidentity, together with Sec. 3, Prop. prop:common-relations (Frobenius grouping by tau), 04-height.tex / 03-arithmetic.tex
issues.description: If the chosen Frobenius lift sigma fixes the labeled field (tau = id on L, i.e. residue field F_p), the paired relation <B,Y(a)P> = <B',Y'(aR)P'> is literally 0=0. So the proposition's claim that 'at least one equation is not an identity' cannot hold for such a group. The proof is still correct, but only vacuously. The diagonal correspondence (multiplier 1, which the finite list includes) sends this case to the exceptional system. There u is the Frobenius endomorphism, and the 4-dimensional marked span T forces conj(pi)=1, which is impossible. So a nonempty tau=id group cannot occur for a marked target. I checked this independently: any nontrivial element of SO_5 fixes at most 3 dimensions. The paper never mentions this case or that it relies on m=1 being in the multiplier list. This is an exposition gap, not a mathematical one.

issues.description: Several load-bearing external inputs are used in exactly the quoted forms, and I did not check them against the sources: Masser-Wustholz endomorphism bounds polynomial in [L:Q] and h_F, the Pazuki theta/Faltings comparison, the crystalline-de Rham comparison over ramified enlargements (Maulik-Poonen / Kubrak-Prikhodko), and the projected path form of Habegger-Pila Cor. 7.2. All are standard and plausibly applied, but correctness depends on those exact forms.

coverage:
I read all six sections and the README. Checks:

- Sec. 1: the rank-5 model, including the q(T) formula and that the lattice is unimodular over Z[1/2]. Also the Goursat/monodromy dichotomy, and finiteness of dominating correspondences via the stabilizer having finite index (finite-area argument).
- Sec. 2: the full interpolation theorem. I checked the zero estimate (row-lattice/minor argument), the graph-fibre codimension-2 lemma, the layer-interpolation condition count against dim V_L, and the product-formula inequalities and order of choices (Q_5 before r, then L, then n).
- Sec. 3: potential good reduction, the denominator ideals, the cross-trace comparison and its integrality, the proximity/factorial cutoff loss, the Frobenius elimination step (sigma rho = rho tau using normality of M), and the tail estimates.
- Sec. 4: the finite-field incidence lemma (T_* construction, all three rank cases, spinor-norm correction), the marking and its saturation, and the lemma lifting reduced isogenies. Also the derivation of I_0 Y(a) = Y'(aR) I_s, the Burnside tensor argument and the single-sign deduction, and exclusion of both signs.
- Sec. 5: the flat-coordinate bounds and the Pila-Zannier dimension count (conic fibres, so dimension at most 2, against the 3-dimensional quadric).

I did not verify the external citations against their sources.
